holidays.name: National Dice Day
holidays.description: A day to roll the bones. Break out your d6s, d20s and board-game dice, and let luck decide your next move. Every roll starts as a mystery until the dice land.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite among tabletop gamers and game-night fans.
holidays.funFact: Dice are among the oldest gaming tools in the world. Six-sided dice have been found at ancient sites that are thousands of years old.

holidays.name: National Sock Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble sock, which keeps toes warm and gets lost in the laundry. Celebrate by wearing your wildest pair or by giving socks to people who need them.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It lands in early winter, when warm feet matter most.
holidays.funFact: Socks are one of the most requested items at homeless shelters, which makes this a good day to donate a few pairs.

holidays.name: Wear Brown Shoes Day
holidays.description: A day to bring brown footwear out of the closet. Loafers, boots and oxfords all count. It's a small tribute to a color that often gets overlooked in favor of black.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is a playful nod to the fashion rule that brown shoes don't belong in certain settings.
holidays.funFact: A long-standing old-school menswear saying claims you should never wear brown in town. Modern style has largely retired that rule.
